days.lesson:
Diabetes mellitus is a chronic disease in which the body cannot properly regulate blood sugar (glucose).
Glucose is the body's main source of energy. It comes from food and enters body cells with the help of a hormone called insulin.
When insulin does not work properly or the body cannot produce enough insulin, glucose builds up in the blood.
Over time, high blood sugar can damage:
• Eyes
• Kidneys
• Nerves
• Heart
• Blood vessels
Key Message:
Diabetes is serious but often preventable.

days.content:
Topic
Signs and Symptoms of Diabetes
Educational Lesson
Common symptoms include:
• Excessive thirst
• Frequent urination
• Excessive hunger
• Unexplained weight loss
• Fatigue
• Blurred vision
Some people experience no symptoms for years.
Interactive Activity
Symptom Recognition Quiz
Symptom Recognition Quiz: Could You Recognize Diabetes Warning Signs?
Instructions: Select the correct answer for each question.
Question 1
Which of the following is a common symptom of diabetes?
A. Increased energy
B. Excessive thirst
C. Better eyesight
D. Reduced appetite
✅ Correct Answer: B. Excessive thirst
Explanation: High blood glucose levels can cause the body to lose more water, leading to increased thirst.

Question 2
A person with diabetes may experience frequent urination because:
A. The body tries to remove excess glucose through urine
B. The person drinks too little water
C. The kidneys stop working immediately
D. The person exercises too much
✅ Correct Answer: A. The body tries to remove excess glucose through urine
Explanation: When blood glucose levels are high, the kidneys work to remove excess sugar, causing frequent urination.

Question 3
Which combination of symptoms may suggest a possible diabetes warning sign?
A. Excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss
B. Increased strength and improved vision
C. Better sleep and increased energy
D. Reduced hunger and weight gain
✅ Correct Answer: A. Excessive thirst, frequent urination, and unexplained weight loss
Explanation: These are common signs that may occur when blood glucose levels are not well controlled.

Question 4
True or False:
"Everyone with Type 2 diabetes will notice symptoms immediately."
A. True
B. False
✅ Correct Answer: B. False
Explanation: Some people with Type 2 diabetes may have no symptoms for years, which is why awareness and regular screening are important.

Remember the warning signs:
💧 Excessive thirst
🚽 Frequent urination
🍽️ Excessive hunger
⚖️ Unexplained weight loss
😴 Fatigue
👁️ Blurred vision
Early recognition can support early testing, prevention, and better health outcomes.

Reflection Question
Have you ever experienced any of these symptoms?
Daily Challenge
Discuss diabetes symptoms with a family member.
Push Notification
"Knowing the signs can help prevent complications."

days.lesson:
Many people believe that diabetes occurs suddenly or only affects older adults. However, Type 2 diabetes develops gradually over several years as a result of a combination of risk factors.
A risk factor is anything that increases the likelihood of developing a disease. Having one or more risk factors does not mean that a person will definitely develop diabetes, but it increases the chances.
Risk factors for Type 2 diabetes can be divided into two categories:
Non-Modifiable Risk Factors:
These are factors that cannot be changed.
1. Family History
People whose parents or siblings have diabetes are at higher risk.
2. Age
Risk generally increases with age, although young adults are increasingly affected.
3. Ethnicity
Certain populations, including many African populations, have higher susceptibility to Type 2 diabetes.

Modifiable Risk Factors:
These are factors that individuals can change.
1. Overweight and Obesity
Excess body fat, especially around the abdomen, increases insulin resistance.
2. Physical Inactivity
Lack of regular exercise reduces the body's ability to use insulin effectively.
3. Unhealthy Diet
Frequent consumption of sugary drinks, fast foods, and highly processed foods contributes to weight gain and diabetes risk.
4. Smoking
Smoking damages blood vessels and increases insulin resistance.
5. Excessive Alcohol Consumption
Heavy alcohol use affects blood glucose regulation and body weight.
Why University Students Should Care:
Many university students experience:
Long hours of sitting during lectures
Frequent consumption of sugary drinks
Irregular meal patterns
High stress levels
Inadequate physical activity
These habits can gradually increase diabetes risk.
Key Takeaway:
Type 2 diabetes often develops silently. Understanding your risk factors allows you to take preventive action early.

days.lesson:
One of the strongest predictors of Type 2 diabetes is family history.
Genes influence how the body:
Produces insulin
Uses insulin
Stores body fat
Regulates blood sugar
If one or both parents have diabetes, your risk is higher than someone without a family history.
However, genetics is not destiny.
Think of genes as loading the gun and lifestyle as pulling the trigger.
A person with a family history who maintains healthy habits may never develop diabetes, while a person without a family history may develop diabetes due to unhealthy lifestyle choices.
Family History Categories:
Low Risk:
No parent or sibling has diabetes.
Moderate Risk:
One close relative has diabetes.
High Risk:
Multiple close relatives have diabetes.
Why Knowing Family History Matters:
Knowing your family history allows you to:
Screen earlier
Improve lifestyle habits
Monitor weight
Seek preventive care
Key Takeaway:
You cannot change your genes, but you can change your lifestyle.

Excess body fat, especially around the waist, increases the risk of developing Type 2 diabetes.
Fat tissue is not just a storage site for energy. It releases substances that affect insulin action.
When excess fat accumulates:
Cells become resistant to insulin.
Blood glucose rises.
The pancreas works harder.
Diabetes risk increases.

Why Waist Size Matters:
Abdominal fat is particularly dangerous because it is strongly associated with insulin resistance.

questions.question: What is a diabetes risk factor?
options: A. Something that guarantees diabetes
B. Anything that increases the likelihood of developing a disease
C. A medicine used to treat diabetes
D. A symptom that only occurs in older adults
questions.correctAnswer: B. Anything that increases the likelihood of developing a disease
questions.explanation: Having a risk factor increases the chance of developing diabetes, but it does not guarantee that it will occur.

questions.question: Can family history increase a person's risk of Type 2 diabetes?
options: A. Yes, having a parent or sibling with diabetes can increase risk
B. No, family history never affects diabetes risk
C. Only friends' health affects risk
D. Only sugary drinks affect risk
questions.correctAnswer: A. Yes, having a parent or sibling with diabetes can increase risk
questions.explanation: Family history is a non-modifiable risk factor, so it cannot be changed but can be considered in prevention planning.

questions.question: Does prolonged sitting increase diabetes risk?
options: A. No, sitting has no effect on health
B. Yes, physical inactivity reduces the body's ability to use insulin effectively
C. Only sitting outdoors increases risk
D. Sitting prevents weight gain
questions.correctAnswer: B. Yes, physical inactivity reduces the body's ability to use insulin effectively
questions.explanation: Breaking up long periods of sitting and being regularly active can help reduce risk.

questions.question: Which pair contains two unhealthy dietary habits that can increase diabetes risk?
options: A. Drinking water and eating vegetables
B. Frequent sugary drinks and fast foods
C. Eating fruit and beans
D. Choosing regular exercise and balanced meals
questions.correctAnswer: B. Frequent sugary drinks and fast foods
questions.explanation: Frequent sugary drinks, fast foods, and highly processed foods can contribute to weight gain and diabetes risk.

questions.question: Can Type 2 diabetes occur in young adults?
options: A. Yes, young adults can develop Type 2 diabetes
B. No, it only affects people over 60
C. No, students cannot develop diabetes
D. Only children can develop Type 2 diabetes
questions.correctAnswer: A. Yes, young adults can develop Type 2 diabetes
questions.explanation: Lifestyle factors can increase Type 2 diabetes risk at younger ages, which makes early prevention important.

Why is portion control important even when eating healthy foods?
A. Healthy foods cannot cause weight gain
B. Eating too much of any food can contribute to weight gain

Explanation: Even nutritious foods can lead to excess calorie intake when eaten in large quantities.

Using the hand-portion method, what is the recommended portion size for carbohydrates?
A. Thumb-sized portion
B. Two handfuls
C. Fist-sized portion
D. Palm-sized portion

B. Candy and biscuits
C. Fruit and groundnuts
D. Cake and sweetened juice
✅ Correct Answer: C. Fruit and groundnuts

How does choosing healthy snacks instead of sugary snacks benefit the body?
A. Causes more hunger between meals
B. Supports better weight control and stable energy levels
C. Increases sugar cravings

Quiz
5 questions.
Question 1
Excessive consumption of sugary foods and drinks can increase the risk of which condition?
A. Improved insulin sensitivity
B. Type 2 diabetes
C. Stronger immunity
D. Faster muscle growth
✅ Correct Answer: B. Type 2 diabetes
Explanation:
Regularly consuming too much sugar can contribute to weight gain, obesity, insulin resistance, and increase the risk of Type 2 diabetes.

Question 2
According to the World Health Organization (WHO), what is the recommended maximum daily intake of added sugar for adults?
A. 2 teaspoons (10 grams)
B. 4 teaspoons (20 grams)
C. 6 teaspoons (25 grams)
D. 10 teaspoons (50 grams)
✅ Correct Answer: C. 6 teaspoons (25 grams)
Explanation:
WHO recommends limiting added sugar intake to about 6 teaspoons or 25 grams per day for adults.

Question 3
Which of the following drinks contains the highest amount of sugar based on the lesson?
A. Coca-Cola
B. Fanta Orange
C. Monster Energy Drink
D. Lucozade Boost
✅ Correct Answer: D. Lucozade Boost
Explanation:
Lucozade Boost contains about 60 grams of sugar, which is approximately 15 teaspoons—far above the recommended daily limit.

Question 4
What happens in the body after consuming a sugary drink?
A. Blood sugar decreases immediately
B. Blood sugar rises rapidly and insulin is released
C. The body stops producing insulin
D. Sugar is removed from the blood instantly
✅ Correct Answer: B. Blood sugar rises rapidly and insulin is released
Explanation:
Sugary drinks cause a rapid increase in blood glucose. The body responds by releasing insulin to help move glucose into cells.

Question 5
Which of the following is a healthier alternative to sugary drinks?
A. Energy drinks
B. Sweetened fruit juice
C. Water or infused water
D. Soft drinks
✅ Correct Answer: C. Water or infused water
Explanation:
Water, infused water, unsweetened tea, and moderate amounts of fresh fruit are healthier options that help reduce excess sugar intake.

B. When calories consumed are greater than calories used by the body

days.lesson:
Food labels provide important information about the foods and drinks you consume. Learning to read food labels can help you make healthier choices, manage your weight, and reduce your risk of developing Type 2 diabetes. Before buying a packaged food, take a few seconds to look at the nutrition label and ingredient list.
The main parts of a food label include:
Serving Size: The amount of food the nutrition information is based on.
Calories: The amount of energy provided in one serving.
Nutrients: Information about carbohydrates, sugars, fats, protein, fibre, sodium, vitamins, and minerals.
Ingredients: Listed from the largest to the smallest amount. Ingredients that appear first are present in the highest quantities.
Why This Matters:
Many packaged foods that seem healthy may contain large amounts of sugar, salt, or unhealthy fats. Reading food labels helps you make informed decisions.

When reading food labels, choose products with lower sodium whenever possible.

Reducing sodium intake supports heart health and lowers the risk of diabetes-related complications.

days.lesson:
Alcohol is a common part of social activities, but it is important to understand how it affects your health. Alcohol provides empty calories, meaning it contains energy but provides little or no essential nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, or fibre.
Regularly consuming large amounts of alcohol can affect your overall health by:
Increasing calorie intake and contributing to weight gain.
Affecting blood sugar control, especially when combined with unhealthy eating habits.
Increasing the risk of chronic diseases such as high blood pressure, heart disease, and Type 2 diabetes.
Alcohol can also affect decision-making, making it harder to maintain healthy lifestyle choices such as choosing nutritious foods or staying physically active.
Why This Matters:
Maintaining a healthy weight and lifestyle reduces your risk of developing Type 2 diabetes. Understanding how alcohol affects your body helps you make informed choices.

Alcohol, Smoking, and Diabetes Risk Quiz (Day 1–5)
Instructions: Choose the best answer for each question.
1. Why is alcohol considered a source of “empty calories”?
A. It contains too much protein
B. It provides energy but little or no essential nutrients
C. It has no effect on body weight
D. It improves blood sugar control
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Alcohol provides calories (energy) but does not provide important nutrients such as vitamins, minerals, or fibre.

2. How can excessive alcohol consumption increase the risk of Type 2 diabetes?
A. By improving insulin sensitivity
B. By increasing physical activity levels
C. By contributing to weight gain and insulin resistance
D. By lowering blood glucose permanently
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Excessive alcohol use can contribute to obesity, liver problems, and insulin resistance, which increase diabetes risk.

A. Improved oxygen delivery
B. Stronger blood vessels
C. Damage to blood vessels and reduced oxygen supply
D. Better blood sugar control
Correct Answer: C
Explanation: Smoking damages blood vessels, reduces oxygen delivery, and increases the risk of heart disease, stroke, and diabetes.

A. When the body uses insulin more effectively
B. When body cells respond poorly to insulin, making glucose control more difficult
C. When the body produces no blood glucose
D. When exercise causes blood sugar to increase
Correct Answer: B
Explanation: Insulin resistance occurs when cells do not respond properly to insulin, making it harder for glucose to enter cells and increasing diabetes risk.

A. These habits only affect older people
B. They have no relationship with diabetes risk
C. Healthy choices during young adulthood can reduce future chronic disease risk

Academic pressure: Exams, assignments, deadlines, and the need to achieve good grades.

Future concerns: Worries about career choices and life after graduation.
While short-term stress can motivate you, long-term stress may affect eating habits, physical activity, sleep, and overall wellbeing.
Why This Matters:
Managing stress effectively can support healthier lifestyle choices and reduce behaviors that increase the risk of weight gain and Type 2 diabetes.

Healthy sleep habits support weight management, emotional wellbeing, and better blood sugar control.

Tips for improving sleep quality include:
Maintain a consistent bedtime: Going to bed and waking up at similar times helps regulate your body clock.
Reduce screen time before bed: Phones, laptops, and other devices can make it harder to fall asleep.
Limit caffeine intake: Drinks such as coffee, energy drinks, and some soft drinks can interfere with sleep, especially when consumed late in the day.
Create a relaxing bedtime routine: Activities such as reading, stretching, or quiet reflection can prepare your body for sleep.
Why This Matters:
Better sleep supports healthier eating habits, energy levels, stress management, and diabetes prevention.

A SMART goal is:
Specific – Clearly state what you want to do.
Measurable – Track your progress.
Achievable – Make sure it is realistic.

Time-bound – Set a deadline.

Why It Matters:
SMART goals increase confidence, improve commitment, and make it easier to build healthy habits over time.

days.lesson:
Changing your lifestyle is a journey, and occasional setbacks are normal. A relapse happens when you return to old habits after making positive changes. Instead of viewing relapse as failure, see it as an opportunity to learn and improve.
The key to long-term diabetes prevention is preparing for challenges before they happen and getting back on track as soon as possible.
Relapse Prevention Strategies:
Plan ahead for busy or stressful periods.
Identify situations that trigger unhealthy choices.
Develop healthier alternatives.
Be flexible and adjust your plans when necessary.
Remember that one unhealthy choice does not erase your progress.
Why It Matters:
Recognizing triggers and responding positively helps you maintain healthy habits and lowers your long-term risk of developing Type 2 diabetes.

days.lesson:
Your surroundings have a powerful influence on your daily choices. Creating an environment that supports healthy living makes it easier to practice positive habits consistently.
Small changes at home, school, or work can reduce temptation and encourage healthier decisions.
Examples of a Healthy Environment:
Keep fruits and healthy snacks within easy reach.
Limit sugary drinks and highly processed snacks.
Use stairs instead of elevators when possible.
Choose walking or cycling for short distances.
Create a regular schedule for meals, sleep, and exercise.
Why It Matters:
A supportive environment helps healthy behaviors become part of your daily routine with less effort.

Congratulations! You have successfully completed the 12-week Diabetes Prevention Programme.
Graduation is not the end of your journey rather it is the beginning of a lifelong commitment to protecting your health. The knowledge and habits you have developed can reduce your risk of Type 2 diabetes and improve your overall well-being for many years to come.
Continue making healthy choices, encourage others to do the same, and remember that every small healthy action makes a difference.

📸 Group photographs and celebration
🤝 Share your experience with fellow participants

🌟 Your Journey Continues
"The end of this program is the beginning of a healthier future. Every healthy choice you continue to make will help protect you from Type 2 diabetes and improve your quality of life for years to come. Remember that progress not perfection is the key to lifelong health. Keep moving, keep learning, and keep choosing health every day."

Diabetes Prevention Champion

Three healthy habits you will continue every day.
Two health goals you want to achieve in the next year.
One trusted person who will support and encourage your healthy lifestyle.
A reminder to review your progress every month.
Congratulations on completing your Diabetes Prevention Journey! Your commitment today is an investment in a healthier future.
